Read the calculation, compare the measures, and keep the assumptions in view.
Published 2026-07-20 · Example updated 2026-10-30 · Illustrative article excerpt
A gain of 50% followed by a loss of 50% leaves less than you started with. The second return acts on a different base.

Start with USD 10,000. The first period raises the balance to USD 15,000. Losing half of that balance in the next period leaves USD 7,500. There are no deposits, withdrawals, fees or taxes in this example.

The arithmetic average is 0%. The total return is −25% over two years. The compound annual return is about −13.4% per year. These measures answer different questions, so the period and unit stay beside the number.

Reordering the same returns does not change the final balance when no cash enters or leaves. Contributions and withdrawals change that relationship. A fixed-rate calculator describes assumptions; it does not predict future returns.
Use the existing tools to examine an annualized return or a contribution schedule. Keep the period, currency and cash-flow assumptions in view.
